40021922.author: पदार्थः
40021922.content: रामस्य of Rama, भाषितम् the speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, परमार्थवित् knower of the highest truth, उवाच spoke, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, वाक्यम् words, राघवम् to Rama, दीप्ततेजसम् radiant with splendor.

40021922.author: Translation
40021922.content: Having heard Rama's speech, Lakshmana, who knew the highest truth, spoke words with folded hands to Rama, who was radiant with splendor.

40021923.author: पदार्थः
40021923.content: अल्पापराधे for a small offense, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, द्विजाभ्याम् by the two Brahmins, शापः a curse, ईदृशः such, महान् severe, नृगस्य of Nṛga, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, यमदण्डः the punishment of Yama, इव like, अपरः another.

40021923.author: Translation
40021923.content: O Kakutstha, for a minor offense, such a severe curse was given by the two Brahmins, like another punishment from Yama for the royal sage Nṛga.

40021924.author: पदार्थः
40021924.content: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, पापसंयुक्तम् associated with sin, आत्मानम् himself, पुरषर्षभ O best of men, किम् what, उवाच did say, नृगः Nṛga, राजा king, द्विजौ to the two Brahmins, क्रोधसमन्वितौ filled with anger.

40021924.author: Translation
40021924.content: O best of men, what did King Nṛga say to the two enraged Brahmins after hearing himself accused of sin?

40021925.author: पदार्थः
40021925.content: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, राघवः Rama, पुनः again, अब्रवीत् said, शृणु listen, सौम्य O gentle one, यथा how, पूर्वम् previously, सः that, राजा king, शापविक्षतः afflicted by the curse.

40021925.author: Translation
40021925.content: When Lakshmana thus spoke, Rama again said, "O gentle one, listen to how that king was previously afflicted by the curse."

40021926.author: पदार्थः
40021926.content: अथ then, अध्वनि on the way, गतौ gone, विप्रौ the two Brahmins, विज्ञाय having known, सः that, नृगः Nṛga, तदा then, आहूय having summoned, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सर्वान् all, नैगमान् citizens, सपुरोधसः along with the priests.

40021926.author: Translation
40021926.content: Then, having understood that the two Brahmins had departed, King Nṛga summoned all his ministers, citizens, and priests.

40021927.author: पदार्थः
40021927.content: तान् to them, उवाच said, नृगः Nṛga, राजा king, सर्वाः all, च and, प्रकृतीः subjects, तथा also, दुःखेन by sorrow, सुसमाविष्टः deeply afflicted, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, मे from me, समाहितैः by those who are attentive.

40021927.author: Translation
40021927.content: Deeply afflicted by sorrow, King Nṛga spoke to all of them, including his subjects, saying, "Let my words be heard by all of you with attention."

40021928.author: पदार्थः
40021928.content: नारदः Narada, पर्वतः Parvata, च and, एव indeed, मम to me, दत्त्वा having given, महत् great, भयम् fear, गतौ have gone, त्रिभुवनम् to the three worlds, भद्रौ the two noble ones, वायुभूतौ having become like wind, अनिन्दितौ the two blameless ones.

40021928.author: Translation
40021928.content: The noble and blameless Narada and Parvata, having instilled great fear in me, have indeed departed to the three worlds, swift as the wind.

40021929.author: पदार्थः
40021929.content: कुमारो अयम् this boy, वसुः नाम by name Vasu, सः he, देवः god, अद्य today, अभिषिच्यताम् let him be consecrated, श्वभ्रम् a pit/cave, च and, यत् which is, सुखस्पर्शम् pleasant to touch, क्रियताम् let it be made, शिल्पिभिः by artisans, मम for me, यत्र where, अहम् I, सङ्क्षयिष्यामि will exhaust/destroy, शापम् the curse, ब्राह्मणनिःसृतम् issued from a Brahmin.

40021929.author: Translation
40021929.content: Let this boy named Vasu be consecrated as a god today, and let artisans construct for me a pleasant cave where I can exhaust the curse issued by a Brahmin.

40021930.author: पदार्थः
40021930.content: वर्षघ्नम् rain-proof, एकम् one, श्वभ्रम् pit/cave, तु indeed, हिमघ्नम् cold-proof, अपरम् another, तथा similarly, ग्रीष्मघ्नम् summer-proof, तु and, सुखस्पर्शम् pleasant to touch, एकम् one, कुर्वन्तु let them make, शिल्पिनः artisans.

40021930.author: Translation
40021930.content: The artisans should construct one cave that is rain-proof, another that is cold-proof, and a third, pleasant to touch, that is summer-proof.

40021931.author: पदार्थः
40021931.content: फलवन्तः fruit-bearing, च and, ये which, वृक्षाः trees, पुष्पवत्यः flower-bearing, च and, या which, लताः creepers, विरोप्यन्ताम् let them be planted, बहुविधाः of many kinds, छायावन्तः shade-giving, च and, गुल्मिनः shrubs.

40021931.author: Translation
40021931.content: Let fruit-bearing trees, flowering creepers, and various kinds of shade-giving shrubs be planted.

40021932.author: पदार्थः
40021932.content: क्रियताम् let it be made, रमणीयम् beautiful, च and, श्वभ्राणाम् of the pits/caves, सर्वतोदिशम् in all directions, सुखम् comfortably, अत्र here, वसिष्यामि I will dwell, यावत् as long as, कालस्य of time, पर्ययः the change/end.

40021932.author: Translation
40021932.content: Let the surroundings of the caves be made beautiful in all directions, for I will dwell there comfortably until the end of my destined time.

40021933.author: पदार्थः
40021933.content: पुष्पाणि flowers, च and, सुगन्धीनि fragrant, क्रियताम् let them be placed/made, तेषु in them, नित्यशः always, परिवार्य surrounding, यथा so that, मे for me, स्युः they may be, अध्यर्धम् one and a half, योजनम् Yojana, तथा thus.

40021933.author: Translation
40021933.content: Let fragrant flowers always be placed in them, surrounding the area for me to a distance of one and a half Yojanas.

40021934.author: पदार्थः
40021934.content: एवं thus, कृत्वा having made, विधानं arrangement, स he, सन्दिदेश instructed, वसं O son, तदा then, धर्मनित्यः ever devoted to dharma, प्रजाः subjects, पुत्र O son, क्षत्रधर्मेण by the duty of a Kshatriya, पालय protect.

40021934.author: Translation
40021934.content: Having made this arrangement, the king then instructed his son, "O son, ever devoted to righteousness, protect your subjects according to the duty of a Kshatriya."

40021935.author: पदार्थः
40021935.content: प्रत्यक्षं directly, ते by you, यथा how, शापो curse, द्विजाभ्यां by the two Brahmins, मयि upon me, पातितः cast, नरश्रेष्ठ O best among men, सरोषाभ्यां by the two angry ones, अपराधे in the offense, अपि even, तादृशे such.

40021935.author: Translation
40021935.content: O best among men, you yourself witnessed how a curse was inflicted upon me by the two angry Brahmins, even for such an offense.

40021936.author: पदार्थः
40021936.content: मा do not, कृथाः make, तनुसन्तापं bodily distress, मत्कृते for my sake, अपि even, नरर्षभ O best of men, कृतान्तः destiny, कुशलः powerful, पुत्र O son, येन by which, अस्मि I am, व्यसनीकृतः made miserable.

40021936.author: Translation
40021936.content: O best of men, do not grieve for my sake, O son, for destiny is powerful, and it is by its force that I have been afflicted with this misery.

40021937.author: पदार्थः
40021937.content: प्राप्तव्यान्येव only those that are to be obtained, प्राप्नोति one obtains, गन्तव्यान्येव only those that are to be gone to, गच्छति one goes, लब्धव्यान्येव only those that are to be received, लभते one receives, दुःखानि sorrows, च and, सुखानि joys, च and.

40021937.author: Translation
40021937.content: One obtains only what is destined to be obtained, goes only where one is destined to go, and receives only the sorrows and joys that are destined to be received.

40021938.author: पदार्थः
40021938.content: पूर्वे in a former, जात्यन्तरे birth, वत्स O son, मा do not, विषादं sorrow, कुरुष्व make, ह indeed.

40021938.author: Translation
40021938.content: O son, do not grieve over what happened in a former birth.

40021939.author: पदार्थः
40021939.content: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, नृपः the king, तत्र there, सुतम् to his son, राजा the king, महायशाः highly renowned, श्वभ्रम् into the well, जगाम went, सुकृतम् well-made, वासाय for dwelling, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men.

40021939.author: Translation
40021939.content: O best among men, having thus spoken to his son, the highly renowned king went into the well, which was well-constructed for his dwelling.

40021940.author: पदार्थः
40021940.content: एवम् thus, प्रविश्यैव having just entered, नृपः the king, तदानीम् at that time, श्वभ्रम् into the well, महारत्नविभूषितम् adorned with great jewels, तत् that, सम्पादयामास he fulfilled, तदा then, महात्मा the great-souled one, शापम् the curse, द्विजाभ्याम् by the two Brahmins, हि indeed, रुषा with anger, विमुक्तम् uttered.

40021940.author: Translation
40021940.content: Having thus just entered that well adorned with great jewels, the great-souled king then fulfilled the curse that had indeed been uttered with anger by the two Brahmins. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 54 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
